item.title: “Dear None”: Questions that Confirm Catholicism as the True Religion, Part 1 - Catholic Exchange
item.description: What belief system truly transforms? Catholic Orthodoxy stands apart from Moralistic Therapeutic Deism, with transcendent reality and purposeful creation.

item.title: The Duty to Rebuke Temerity - Catholic Exchange
item.description: Secular media defends a pro-abortion coach while slandering the bishop upholding Church teaching. True charity rebukes temerity and protects the unborn.

item.title: The Seat of Moses and the Crucifixion of Christ - Catholic Exchange
item.description: Jesus affirms the seat of Moses yet rebukes Pharisaic hypocrisy. Authority flows from covenant, not pride, and humility is exalted in the Kingdom.

item.title: “Dear None”: Questions that Confirm Catholicism as the True Religion, Part 2 - Catholic Exchange
item.description: Six inescapable questions distinguish Catholic Orthodoxy from Modernism, Islam, Judaism, Calvinism, and Lutheranism. Only one path leads to full sanctity.

item.title: How to Deal with Pain - Catholic Exchange
item.description: Christ taught us how to die by first showing how to live fully in joy and mercy. His pain on the Cross turns sorrow into redemption and freedom.

item.title: Finish Lent Strong - Catholic Exchange
item.description: Lent’s early zeal often fades, but the final weeks matter most. Perseverance through fatigue forms true holiness as we walk with Christ to Calvary.

item.title: Jean Louis Berlandier and the Pious Witness of America - Catholic Exchange
item.description: What turned a skeptical scientist into a lay missionary? Berlandier’s travels, healings, and love for creation led him to serve all people as a witness to God’s goodness.

item.title: Why People Fall from Faith & the Fear of Accepting God - Catholic Exchange
item.description: Atheists and agnostics frequently cite science or humanism as the reason for their rejection of God, yet the real root lies deeper: fear and control.

item.title: Doing God’s Work Doesn’t Mean He Owes Us - Catholic Exchange
item.description: Post-mission exhaustion and illness exposed the illusion of immediate reward. But in our frailty, we are reminded that grace alone proves sufficient.

item.title: Jim Meads and the Monster Weed - Catholic Exchange
item.description: Jim’s final weed-pulling battle ended with God catching his fall. His life teaches us to confront soul-weeds with total effort and trust in divine arms.

item.title: Vegetarianism and the Great Commission - Catholic Exchange
item.description: Vegetarianism as mission work: one Catholic lives out Christ’s command by honoring the sanctity of all life, seeing God’s love reflected in every creature.

item.title: Cultivating the Garden of Our Souls - Catholic Exchange
item.description: “When will I stop needing Confession?” The garden teaches patience with ourselves. Weeds reappear, but diligent, humble care allows flowers to bloom for the Lord.

item.title: Salesian Spirituality for Lent: Fostering Perpetual Renewal - Catholic Exchange
item.description: St. Francis de Sales' final counsels of Introduction to the Devout Life emphasize perseverance, ordinary actions, and keeping heaven in view.

item.title: Not a Sympathetic Villain: Judas' Betrayal - Catholic Exchange
item.description: Can we pity Judas? Scripture shows his conscious decision after Christ’s clear warning. Mercy awaited him, as it did Peter, but only humble contrition receives it.

item.title: Holy Week Was Political—And It Still Is - Catholic Exchange
item.description: The Passion unfolded at the intersection of law, religion, and empire. Christ’s refusal to conform makes Him dangerous to every age that values power over truth.
